\chapter{What You Wear}
\label{ch:ml-clothing}
\hlchaptermodality{100}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can name what someone is wearing, and call it new or old.}

From cold: four things worn, two endings between them, and an adjective that has not moved since chapter 42.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[muṇṭŭ]{\ml{മുണ്ട്} (muṇṭŭ) — a mundu}

\label{lesson:ML-C100-mundu}



\begin{quote}
Say the word for \emph{cloth}. Then say \emph{new}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\textbf{\ml{മുണ്ട്}} — \emph{muṇṭŭ} — \textbf{a mundu}, the length of cloth worn wrapped at the waist.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{ഇത്} \ml{പുതിയ} \ml{മുണ്ടാണ്}.} — \emph{itŭ putiya muṇṭāṇŭ} — \textquotedblleft{}This is a new mundu.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{The book gave you the cloth before it gave you the garment.} \textbf{\ml{തുണി}} is the stuff; \textbf{\ml{മുണ്ട്}} is the thing made of it and worn.

Two things in that sentence you already know how to do, and neither is new:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textbf{\ml{പുതിയ}} sits in front and does not change — that is the whole adjective pattern from the chapter that taught it.
  \item \textbf{\ml{മുണ്ട്}} ends in the breathed half-u, so \textbf{\ml{ആണ്}} lands straight on it: \textbf{\ml{മുണ്ടാണ്}}, nothing slid in — the same join \textbf{\ml{പാട്ട്}} takes.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{So the only new thing here is the word itself.}
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{muṇṭŭ}
  \item \emph{itŭ putiya muṇṭāṇŭ}
  \item \emph{pāṭṭāṇŭ}, then \emph{muṇṭāṇŭ}, and hear the same landing
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What is \emph{a mundu}? (\textbf{\ml{മുണ്ട്}}.) Where does \textbf{\ml{പുതിയ}} go, and does it change? (\textbf{In front, and no}.) What slides in before \textbf{\ml{ആണ്}}? (\textbf{Nothing} — \textbf{\ml{മുണ്ടാണ്}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[sāri]{\ml{സാരി} (sāri) — a sari}

\label{lesson:ML-C100-saari}



\begin{quote}
Say \emph{a mundu}. Then say \emph{old}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\textbf{\ml{സാരി}} — \emph{sāri} — \textbf{a sari.}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{ഇത്} \ml{പഴയ} \ml{സാരിയാണ്}.} — \emph{itŭ paḻaya sāriyāṇŭ} — \textquotedblleft{}This is an old sari.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{Two garments, two different landings.} \textbf{\ml{മുണ്ട്}} ends in the half-u and takes \textbf{\ml{ആണ്}} straight on. \textbf{\ml{സാരി}} ends in \textbf{\ml{ഇ}}, and you know what \textbf{\ml{ഇ}} does:

\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{word} & \textbf{joined to \textbf{\ml{ആണ്}}} \\
\midrule
\textbf{\ml{മുണ്ട്}} & \textbf{\ml{മുണ്ടാണ്}} (\emph{muṇṭāṇŭ}) \\
\textbf{\ml{സാരി}} & \textbf{\ml{സാരിയാണ്}} (\emph{sāriyāṇŭ}) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

The \textbf{\ml{യ}} in \textbf{\ml{സാരിയാണ്}} is the one \textbf{\ml{കളി}} and \textbf{\ml{ഭംഗി}} take, for the reason you were given then: \textbf{\ml{ഇ}} calls for it.

\textbf{\ml{പഴയ}} behaves as \textbf{\ml{പുതിയ}} did — in front, unchanged.
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{sāri}
  \item \emph{itŭ paḻaya sāriyāṇŭ}
  \item \emph{muṇṭāṇŭ}, then \emph{sāriyāṇŭ}, and hear which one gains a letter
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What is \emph{a sari}? (\textbf{\ml{സാരി}}.) \textbf{\ml{സാരി}} ends in \textbf{\ml{ഇ}} — what slides in before \textbf{\ml{ആണ്}}? (\textbf{\ml{യ}} — \textbf{\ml{സാരിയാണ്}}.) And \textbf{\ml{മുണ്ട്}}? (\textbf{Nothing} — \textbf{\ml{മുണ്ടാണ്}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ceruppŭ]{\ml{ചെരുപ്പ്} (ceruppŭ) — a sandal}

\label{lesson:ML-C100-cheruppu}



\begin{quote}
Say \emph{a sari}. Then say \emph{a mundu}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\textbf{\ml{ചെരുപ്പ്}} — \emph{ceruppŭ} — \textbf{a sandal}, the everyday open footwear.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{ഇത്} \ml{പഴയ} \ml{ചെരുപ്പാണ്}.} — \emph{itŭ paḻaya ceruppāṇŭ} — \textquotedblleft{}This is an old sandal.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{This word is not a garment, and the book wants both.} \textbf{\ml{മുണ്ട്}} and \textbf{\ml{സാരി}} go on the body; \textbf{\ml{ചെരുപ്പ്}} goes on the feet.

Its ending you have already handled twice. \textbf{\ml{ചെരുപ്പ്}} finishes in the breathed half-u, like \textbf{\ml{മുണ്ട്}}, so \textbf{\ml{ആണ്}} lands straight on it: \textbf{\ml{ചെരുപ്പാണ്}}.

\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{word} & \textbf{joined to \textbf{\ml{ആണ്}}} \\
\midrule
\textbf{\ml{മുണ്ട്}} & \textbf{\ml{മുണ്ടാണ്}} (\emph{muṇṭāṇŭ}) \\
\textbf{\ml{ചെരുപ്പ്}} & \textbf{\ml{ചെരുപ്പാണ്}} (\emph{ceruppāṇŭ}) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{ceruppŭ}
  \item \emph{itŭ paḻaya ceruppāṇŭ}
  \item \emph{muṇṭāṇŭ}, then \emph{ceruppāṇŭ}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What is \emph{a sandal}? (\textbf{\ml{ചെരുപ്പ്}}.) What slides in before \textbf{\ml{ആണ്}}? (\textbf{Nothing} — \textbf{\ml{ചെരുപ്പാണ്}}.) Which other word here does the same? (\textbf{\ml{മുണ്ട്}} — \textbf{\ml{മുണ്ടാണ്}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[toppi]{\ml{തൊപ്പി} (toppi) — a cap}

\label{lesson:ML-C100-thoppi}



\begin{quote}
Say \emph{a sandal}. Then say \emph{new}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\textbf{\ml{തൊപ്പി}} — \emph{toppi} — \textbf{a cap.}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{ഇത്} \ml{പുതിയ} \ml{തൊപ്പിയാണ്}.} — \emph{itŭ putiya toppiyāṇŭ} — \textquotedblleft{}This is a new cap.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{Four things worn, and only two endings between them.} \textbf{\ml{തൊപ്പി}} ends in \textbf{\ml{ഇ}}, so it joins the way \textbf{\ml{സാരി}} does:

\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{ends in} & \textbf{word} & \textbf{joined to \textbf{\ml{ആണ്}}} \\
\midrule
half-u & \textbf{\ml{മുണ്ട്}} & \textbf{\ml{മുണ്ടാണ്}} (\emph{muṇṭāṇŭ}) \\
half-u & \textbf{\ml{ചെരുപ്പ്}} & \textbf{\ml{ചെരുപ്പാണ്}} (\emph{ceruppāṇŭ}) \\
\textbf{\ml{ഇ}} & \textbf{\ml{സാരി}} & \textbf{\ml{സാരിയാണ്}} (\emph{sāriyāṇŭ}) \\
\textbf{\ml{ഇ}} & \textbf{\ml{തൊപ്പി}} & \textbf{\ml{തൊപ്പിയാണ്}} (\emph{toppiyāṇŭ}) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

\textbf{Nothing in this chapter asked you to learn a join.} Both were already yours — the half-u from the song word, the \textbf{\ml{യ}} from the game and the beauty words. What the chapter gave you is four things to wear.
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{toppi}
  \item \emph{itŭ putiya toppiyāṇŭ}
  \item the four joined forms in the table, one after another
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What is \emph{a cap}? (\textbf{\ml{തൊപ്പി}}.) \textbf{\ml{തൊപ്പി}} ends in \textbf{\ml{ഇ}} — what slides in before \textbf{\ml{ആണ്}}? (\textbf{\ml{യ}} — \textbf{\ml{തൊപ്പിയാണ്}}.) Which other worn thing ends the same way? (\textbf{\ml{സാരി}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[muṇṭuṁ sāriyuṁ enna ōrmma]{(a mundu, a sari, a sandal, a cap) — from cold}

\label{lesson:ML-R100-clothing-recall}



\begin{quote}
Close the lessons before this one. Say \emph{a mundu}, \emph{a sari}, \emph{a sandal}, \emph{a cap}.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: two endings, and an adjective that never moves}]
Four things to wear, and \textbf{between them only two endings}:

\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{ends in} & \textbf{word} & \textbf{joined to \textbf{\ml{ആണ്}}} \\
\midrule
half-u & \textbf{\ml{മുണ്ട്}} & \textbf{\ml{മുണ്ടാണ്}} (\emph{muṇṭāṇŭ}) \\
half-u & \textbf{\ml{ചെരുപ്പ്}} & \textbf{\ml{ചെരുപ്പാണ്}} (\emph{ceruppāṇŭ}) \\
\textbf{\ml{ഇ}} & \textbf{\ml{സാരി}} & \textbf{\ml{സാരിയാണ്}} (\emph{sāriyāṇŭ}) \\
\textbf{\ml{ഇ}} & \textbf{\ml{തൊപ്പി}} & \textbf{\ml{തൊപ്പിയാണ്}} (\emph{toppiyāṇŭ}) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

\textbf{Neither join was new.} The half-u one arrived with the song word; the \textbf{\ml{യ}} arrived with the game and the beauty words. This chapter spent all four of its words on things, and none on grammar.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{ഇത്} \ml{പുതിയ} \ml{മുണ്ടാണ്}.} — \emph{itŭ putiya muṇṭāṇŭ} — this is a new mundu.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{ഇത്} \ml{പഴയ} \ml{സാരിയാണ്}.} — \emph{itŭ paḻaya sāriyāṇŭ} — this is an old sari.
\end{quote}

\textbf{\ml{പുതിയ}} and \textbf{\ml{പഴയ}} sit in front and do not change — the same shape they had in the chapter that taught them, with no ending added for the noun that follows.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{muṇṭŭ}, \emph{sāri}, \emph{ceruppŭ}, \emph{toppi}
  \item \emph{itŭ putiya muṇṭāṇŭ}, then \emph{itŭ paḻaya ceruppāṇŭ}
  \item the word for the cloth a \textbf{\ml{മുണ്ട്}} is made of
  \item which two of the four gain a \textbf{\ml{യ}}, and what they end in
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A mundu, a sari, a cap? (\textbf{\ml{മുണ്ട്}, \ml{സാരി}, \ml{തൊപ്പി}}.) Which of the three takes \textbf{nothing} before \textbf{\ml{ആണ്}}? (\textbf{\ml{മുണ്ട്}} — it ends in the half-u.) And where does \textbf{\ml{പുതിയ}} stand? (\textbf{In front, unchanged}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
